findings.description: お邪魔なようでしたら失礼いたします means if he is unwelcome he will leave; I apologize if I am disturbing you substitutes an apology. Battler’s following response likewise treats it as saying sorry rather than departing.

contexts.japanese:
「あんたが、俺に引導を渡しに来たのかい」
「………そのようなことはございません。
……お邪魔なようでしたら失礼いたします」
「…おいおい、用件も伝えず失礼しますじゃ、かえって気持ち悪いぜ。
…何の用だよ。
contexts.japanesePC: ……お邪魔なようでしたら失礼いたします。」

「あんたが、俺に引導を渡しに来たのかい」

……お邪魔なようでしたら失礼いたします」

…何の用だよ。
contexts.WH: ......I apologize if I am disturbing you."
contexts.MG:
"Did you come to give me my last rites?"
"......Nothing of the sort.
...I apologize if I am disturbing you."
"...Hey, hey, saying I'm sorry without even telling me what you want is actually pretty creepy.
...What do you want?
contexts.UP:
"Did you come to give me my last rites?"
".........Nothing of the sort.
......I shall excuse myself if I am disturbing you."
"...Wait, wait, excusing yourself without even telling me what you wanted would actually just be creepy.
...What do you want?
contexts.note: MG retains I apologize if I am disturbing you and Battler responds to an apology. UP says I shall excuse myself and Battler responds to Genji leaving without stating his business.

MG.japanese: 「………そのようなことはございません。……お邪魔なようでしたら失礼いたします」

findings.sourceReading: Genji offers to withdraw if he is disturbing Battler, who objects to his leaving without saying what he came for.
findings.alternative: 失礼 can be apologetic, but the conditional departure and Battler’s response identify its function here.

contexts.MG:
He thought the shapeless murderer, or maybe the Golden Witch, might come to kill him now that he was isolated,
but he no longer had any desire to resist.
He didn't even feel like using a locked door to hold off the culprit.
He wanted that person to come at him openly, from the front.
...If it was the killer, he wanted to ask them about some of those wonderful closed room tricks as a parting gift.
If it was the witch, he hoped she'd at least take his life with some spectacular magic.
...However, ironically, neither of these two came to meet him...
contexts.UP:
He did think that maybe the shapeless murderer, or the Golden Witch, might come to kill him now that he was isolated,
but he no longer thought about resisting that.
On the contrary, he had no intention of blocking the culprit with a lock.
He wanted that person to come at him openly, from the front.
...If it was a murderer, he thought he'd ask them to tell about some of those wonderful locked room tricks as a parting souvenir.
And if it was a witch, he thought he'd ask her to at least take his life with some wonderful magic.
......However, ironically, neither of these two came to meet Battler...

UP.japanese: 別に鍵は掛けていない。姿なき殺人犯、もしくは黄金の魔女が、一人ぼっちになった自分を殺しに来るかもしれないと思ったが、それに抗おうとはもう思わなかった。
UP.translation: He hadn't bothered to lock it. He did think that maybe the shapeless murderer, or the Golden Witch, might come to kill him now that he was isolated, but he no longer thought about resisting that.

findings.sourceReading: Battler contrasts the unseen murderer with the Golden Witch and hopes that, if it is the witch, she will take his life with spectacular magic.
findings.alternative: 魔女 can be generic without an article in Japanese, and the following feminine pronoun still evokes the expected witch.

findings.description: MG preserves the longer original-PC drinking exchange: the underage-drinking remark, Battler drinking to cope without tasting the alcohol, Genji asking whether he devotes his final moments to drink, and Kinzo as a heavy drinker drowning his cares. The maintained PS3-derived Japanese rewrites this around idle use of Battler's remaining time, readiness to die, and Kinzo as larger-than-life. These MG details are yellow original-PC material and excluded from the error count.

that you would spend the little time you have left drinking?"
Those words...pierced me...

contexts.UP:

......Of course it wasn't.
"...............................

......I'm ready to die at any time..."
"......You are just like the Master.

".........The Master's life,

"...Hey, hey, saying I'm sorry without even telling me what you want is actually pretty creepy. ...What do you want? ...Are you gonna tell me that drinking alcohol is forbidden for minors? I'll just die anyway.` ...Please, let me do what I want, now that it's all about to end." 
"......Battler-sama, do you love alcohol so much... that you would spend the little time you have left drinking?" 
Those words...pierced me... ...That wasn't true. 
"............... I just...can't cope if I don't drink. ...I can't even taste the alcohol at all..." 
"...You are just like the Master. Indeed, you inherited the Master's blood strongly..." 
"You mean Grandfather, the heavy drinker, was drinking to drown his sorrows the whole time...? First I've heard of it." 
......After a number of sad incidents, the Master's life... was reduced to one of atonement alone."

findings.sourceNote: Original Witch Hunt is compared with the original-PC Japanese embedded in the historical patches. The MangaGamer and PS3 witnesses are not independently certified retail extractions.

findings.description: MG's alcohol and appropriate liquor preserve original-PC 酒 and お酒. The maintained PS3-derived Japanese broadens these references to 飲み物 and omits an explicit alcohol noun, which UP follows with something. The specificity is yellow original-PC material and excluded from the error count.
